attestations.reason: The guard refuses a rendering Parse reads as a different file. Every File reachable through Parse or built by hand renders to its own form: lists are cloned and sorted, an empty enable kept distinct from an absent one, scalars spelled plain only where the parser itself reads them back as that text, and what Parse rejects is refused a line earlier. No input reaches the guard's refusal; it holds the emitter to the reader against drift between the two, and a test needs an emitter fault to observe it.

A severity is one of the words error and warning, which the scalar rule spells plain; passing them through it changes no rendering. The rule is applied so the clause holds for every emitted scalar should the severity domain widen, and Parse refuses any other value before the rendering.

checkLimits refuses a Spec with any zero limit before New, and sandbox's contract reports AccountingNone only when no limit was stated, so a bounded run never reaches this branch with AccountingNone; the guard is the runtime check of the Structural-check gate over a state the seam cannot construct

Equivalent: Deterministic governs map-field ordering only, and neither CodeGeneratorRequest nor the descriptor protos it carries declare a map field, so the wire bytes are identical either way (TestGenRequestDeterministic pins the byte-identity across runs). The flag stays as the declared intent of REQ-gen-request-determinism.

A version base's pin is recorded by the client at acquisition and the archive it verified is the archive parsed, so no path materializes a pin and then fails; a reference base records no pin; and every earlier module's pins were saved by their own iteration. A failure therefore never leaves an unsaved pin, and the save on the failure path is the discipline's shape, not a reachable difference.

Equivalent by construction: entryKind hands every non-file, non-link mode — a directory's included — to its submodule arm, so kind == KindFile is already false for a directory entry named like the module file; the guard states the intent (a directory is no module file) rather than adding a decision, and no test can distinguish the two.

the store is constructed with the verification seam (ocifs.WithVerifier) and runs it on every Pull, so a pull that returned without the seam setting resolved is unreachable through this acquirer; the guard mirrors Acquire's and exists so a seamless store could never yield an override
